In 4-dimensional [[geometry]], the '''icosahedral bipyramid''' is the [[direct sum]] of an [[icosahedron]] and a segment, {{nowrap|{3,5} + { }.}} Each face of a central icosahedron is attached with two [[tetrahedra]], creating 40 tetrahedral cells, 80 triangular faces, 54 edges, and 14 vertices.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bendwavy.org/klitzing/incmats/ikedpy.htm | title=Ite }}</ref> An icosahedral bipyramid can be seen as two [[icosahedral pyramid]]s augmented together at their [[Base (geometry)|bases]].

It is the dual of a [[dodecahedral prism]], [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]] {{CDD|node_1|2|node_1|3|node|5|node}}, so the bipyramid can be described as {{CDD|node_f1|2x|node_f1|3|node|5|node}}. Both have [[Coxeter notation]] symmetry [2,3,5], order 240.

Having all regular cells (tetrahedra), it is a [[Blind polytope]].
